rule.why: The Join rule attaches all knowledge to the RE, so the next agent finds a memory where the goal it serves is borne, and memory cannot tell an RE from a PE for you.

rules.rule: Record each memory at the RE whose goal it serves, never at a PE that provides for it.

prompts.connect: – memory: read and record what happened in the work at a node, on its RE
prompts.instructions: Follow these steps for each interaction: 1. Project Identification: - You should assume that you are working on {project} 2. Element Identification: - This is {this.address} ({this.name}) or any other address you work on for this session. 3. Memory Retrieval: - Always begin your work by saying only "Remembering..." and retrieve all relevant information from your knowledge graph: everything at the element's address and everything it inherits from the addresses below it toward the trunk, then search_nodes and open_nodes for what that leads to - Always refer to your knowledge graph as your "memory" 4. Memory and Knowledge - While working on the project, be attentive to any new information, and tell which it is: a) Memory: what happened in the work: what was done, tried, decided, found broken or fixed, and the lessons it taught b) Knowledge: what is now known to be true of the project: what an element is and the files that realize it, how it behaves and fails, the constraints and choices that hold for it, the purpose it serves, the elements it receives from and provides to, and its genre, style, medium and encoding, which the base map leaves out 5. Memory Update: - If any memory was gathered during the work, update your memory as follows: a) Create entities with create_entities for significant events, decisions, defects and lessons: each with a unique name, an entityType and its observations, at the address it concerns b) Connect them to the current entities using create_relations: from, to, and a relationType in active voice c) Store facts about them as observations with add_observations, one fact per observation 6. Knowledge Update: - If any knowledge was gathered during the work, add it to the map's knowledge layers as follows: a) Any address that does not exist yet can be created: add the element or join the work shows the map lacks with map knowledge add-element and add-join; naming a new element makes a new layer for it b) Record what is known at the address where you found it to hold, with map knowledge add-property or add-item, including its genre, style, medium and encoding c) Correct any element or join that is wrong with map refine
prompts.instructions_unassigned: This is the address of the element you are working on at any given time.
prompts.recorded_unjoined: Recorded in the whole memory graph, at no node.
prompts.recorded_nothing: Nothing new to record: each memory and observation was held already.
prompts.stale: STALE: . Check it against the code before relying on this memory.
prompts.locked_read: LOCKED: every agent reads this memory and none can change or delete it; only the person unlocks it.
prompts.stale_counts: Stale = a memory whose cited file or lines changed since it was written; read it before relying on it: metaform memory read_graph node=<address>
